title: Vivarium for Godot 4 is live: butterflies, koi, frogs and fireflies your maps fill themselves with
html:
Vivarium is live for Godot 4. Point it at your TileMapLayer and it fills what is on screen with the small life the place would have: 48 species in 10 families, by biome and by time of day. Butterflies and bees on the meadow, dragonflies over the pond, koi under it, frogs on the bank that dive when the player walks up, lizards basking on the path, and at night moths round the lamp, fireflies and bats. No image file ships; every wing, fin and leg is painted by GDScript into one texture when a level loads.

What it does

  • Vivarium2D reads each tile: a vivarium custom data value, or the tile's collision (a wall or a tree trunk holds nothing). Water gets fish, skaters and dragonflies; the bank gets frogs; open ground gets butterflies, bees and lizards. 8 biomes decide the cast.
  • Day, dusk and night come from an hour you set or from your CanvasModulate tint, so a day and night cycle you already have drives it. Fireflies glow on their own layer above the dark.
  • Creatures flee from the player, settle, bask, dive and circle the lamp; flyers cast soft ground shadows.
  • VivariumColony2D places one species by hand; each of the 48 species ships as a ready colony scene.

Tested

  • Every species photographed under Forward+ and Compatibility: 96 frames, zero engine errors, all 48 distinct.
  • The shipped zip installed into a blank Godot 4.7.2 project under both renderers: Vivarium2D on a TileMapLayer by custom data and by collision, a colony preset, a custom species, zones, water layers, day, dusk and night, fleeing and diving.
  • 7 attacks, including a path with spaces and non Latin characters, fifty colonies and a dense map on screen at once, a third renderer, bad inputs and a renamed addon folder; 196 Readme claims checked against the shipped files.
  • Looking at the pictures found what no counter could: firefly glow swallowing the beetle, bees that read as striped eggs, a moth whose wing pattern landed outside its wing, a field guide whose text drew as boxes, and a whirligig beetle that looked like a target. All were redrawn before release.
  • The stress test found two faults in the code itself. Every flyer's ground shadow was a shape rebuilt each frame, which cost Forward+ 33 to 34 ms a frame in two runs with 346 creatures on screen; drawn as one shared texture it measured 2 to 6 ms in three. And phase() could lag behind a time of day you had just set; it now updates the moment you set it.

Free lite

The page carries a free MIT lite: 12 of the 48 species, the same nodes and the demo.

Where this line stands: 20 Godot packs live from this studio, 1 purchase so far (read from the store the day this went live).

Disclosure: the scripts, the species painters and the demo were written with AI; the cover illustration was made by an AI image model.
